title: Speed vs Fidelity — Quantization Lab & Console Walkthrough
summary: Intro demo focused on quantization tradeoffs (INT8 vs FP8), using Redwood Console Optimize suggestions, and a quick live micro-benchmark. Customer is evaluating for clinical summarization pipeline; main concerns are latency, hallucination risk after aggressive quant, and ability to run tests in a dedicated pilot.

Next steps: pilot scope and benchmark plan

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (CTO), Dana (ML Eng), Ben (Infra)
Links referenced: demo slides https://redwood.ai/sales/deck-quant-lab (internal), sample notebook link: https://redwood.ai/notebooks/quant-benchmark (shared), security brief: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros — I'm Maya on AE, and Jordan will run the deep bits. Samir, Dana, Ben — want to do quick intros?
[00:10] Samir: Sure — Samir here, CTO at Blueline. We're looking at serving rodent — I mean, sorry, medical summarization models for discharge notes, low-latency is big, but we can't sacrifice accuracy.
[00:22] Dana: Dana, lead ML. We're currently on MegaCloud endpoints, running a 13B open model, about 180ms p50, 520ms p95, cost is climbing. We're curious if int8 or fp8 will get us under 100ms p50 without regressions.
[00:37] Ben: Ben infra — security and VPC questions mainly.
[00:40] Jordan: Great. Today's agenda: quick console walkthrough of Optimize -> quant profiles, explanation of INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, a live microbenchmark using a 512 token workload, and then discuss pilot scope.
[00:50] Priya: heads up — audio might clip a bit when I screen share.
[00:54] Dana: no problem.

[01:05] Jordan: I'm sharing my screen. Slide one is a visual: think of quantization as shrinking weights; INT8 cuts to 8-bit integers, FP8 keeps small floating dynamic range. INT8 is typically cheaper and faster on many runtimes, FP8 can preserve some distribution tails and often has fewer quality regressions on certain layers.
[01:30] Samir: slow down — when you say "fewer regressions" — can you quantify?
[01:36] Jordan: Yeah, fair. In our internal benchmarks for summarization-like prompts on the Redwood-13B variant, INT8 introduced a tiny delta in rouge-like metrics, about 0.8–1.5 points in our test set when we used a default symmetric quantization; FP8 saw ~0.2–0.6 delta. But caveat: those numbers vary a lot per model architecture and the prompt distribution.
[01:58] Dana: So FP8 is closer to float32 but a bit slower and more memory?
[02:03] Jordan: Roughly, yes. FP8 preserves dynamic range better so you often avoid clipping rare, high-valued weights. Performance depends on kernel support on the hardware and our runtime — on some GPUs FP8 paths are optimized, on others they fall back and are slower than INT8.

[02:25] [Jordan switches to Redwood Console: Optimize -> Quant Profiles]
[02:30] Jordan: This is our Optimize tab. You can create a quant profile that targets latency, cost, or quality. See the policy slider — we set it to "balanced" for this demo. The console also auto-suggests per-layer exceptions if a regression is detected.
[02:48] Dana: How do you detect regressions? Is it token-level or end-metric?
[02:53] Jordan: We hook into your eval harness — you upload a prompt set and metrics. Our backend runs A/B tests across candidate quant profiles and reports delta on configured metrics, plus we show failure cases (where the generation diverges beyond thresholds).
[03:08] Maya: And you can pin safe-guards — for example, force FP8 on attention layers if you see hallucination regressions.
[03:16] Dana: Interesting.

[03:28] [04:00] Jordan: Now the live microbench. We'll run three variants: FP32 baseline hosted, INT8 profile, and FP8 profile. Each is a single-shot throughput measurement on a 512-token medical-summary prompt. Note: the hosted runtime for this demo is a Redwood-hosted dev cluster; dedicated performance may be slightly better.
[04:22] Ben: Can you make sure to log p50/p95? p95 is our real pain.
[04:26] Jordan: Will do. Starting FP32 baseline run...
[04:35] [05:10] Jordan: Baseline results: p50 210ms, p95 590ms, token throughput x1. Now INT8 run…
[05:18] Jordan: INT8 results: p50 95ms, p95 280ms, token throughput x2.2. Visual note: we saw some token-deletion events in the outputs on ~6% of prompts (shorter summaries with missing clinical detail).
[05:40] Dana: That's the worry. Losing clinical detail could be risky for us.
[05:44] Jordan: Understood. Now FP8 run results: p50 120ms, p95 330ms, token throughput x1.7. Quality regressions were observed at ~1.3% of prompts, mostly minor paraphrase differences.
[06:05] Samir: So INT8 is fastest but has a larger failure mode. FP8 is a middle ground.
[06:11] Jordan: Exactly. Also worth noting we can do hybrid profiles — INT8 for MLP layers, FP8 for attention, or per-layer exceptions automatically suggested by Optimize.

[06:30] [06:45] Priya: I'll pull up the suggested per-layer map — you'll see flagged layers in red where our eval detected high divergence and recommend FP8 for those.
[06:55] Dana: How many prompts did you run for this quick test?
[06:58] Jordan: This demo used a 100-sample prompt subset. For pilot, we recommend 2–5k prompts stratified by the hard cases.

[07:10] Ben: From infra side — for dedicated, what GPU families do you recommend? We have A100s and a cluster with H100s planned.
[07:18] Jordan: H100 can give better FP8 support depending on software stack; A100 INT8 is rock-solid. Our runtime has optimized kernels for H100 FP8, and we can show kernel-level logs after the pilot.

[07:38] [08:00] Dana: What about fallback behaviors in production? If we roll INT8 and see a spike in regressions, can traffic be automatically routed to FP8 or baseline?
[08:07] Maya: Yes — Console supports rollout policies, canary thresholds, and automatic fallback to a compatible model/profile. You can set strict SLOs that trigger automatic rollback and notify owners.
[08:19] Samir: Nice. And the canary traffic split — can we route by token-length or by customer?
[08:24] Jordan: Both. Routing rules can be configured by header, route, token length, or arbitrary attributes you pass in.

[08:40] [09:05] (Small cross-talk, someone sneezes)
[09:10] Dana: On the quality side, does Redwood provide synthetic adversarial prompts or do we need to supply those?
[09:16] Jordan: We have a library of adversarial patterns and clinical-specific checks that we can seed, but your production data is the best test. We recommend you supply edge-case prompts; we'll augment with adversarial sets.

[09:35] [10:00] Jordan: Quick dive into per-token cost math — INT8 saves memory bandwidth and compute cycles so your per-token cost drops; FP8 is in between. Our Console shows estimated cost delta per 1M tokens given your traffic profile; you can preview for different profiles.
[10:15] Dana: Can that cost preview factor in caching — e.g., KV cache hits for multi-turn?
[10:19] Jordan: Yes — you can specify your session length distribution and caching hit rates; the estimate recalculates.

[10:35] [11:00] Samir: Security question — if we go dedicated or private, does quantization happen in our environment or at Redwood before shipping artifacts?
[11:08] Maya: For Hosted, quantization occurs in our runtime. For Dedicated and Private deployments, you can choose to run the Optimize tooling inside your VPC — we provide an offline quantization toolchain that runs inside customer infra and outputs profiles that you keep control of.
[11:25] Ben: Good — we prefer the quant artifacts to be generated in our environment for compliance reasons.

[11:50] [12:15] Jordan: Now I'll demo the Audit logs and evaluation diff view — here's a prompt where INT8 dropped a medically-relevant phrase. You can click into the diff, see the tokens where divergence exceeds threshold, and opt to pin FP8 for the offending layer.
[12:40] Dana: Can we get automated unit-test style alerts? E.g., if any new model roll increases a certain failure rate?
[12:46] Jordan: Yes — we integrate with your CI and will fail a rollout if configured thresholds are exceeded. We also can send alerts to Slack or webhook.

[13:10] [13:45] Maya: Let's talk timeline. What would you need to run a pilot?
[13:48] Samir: We'd need realistic prompt sets, baseline metrics, and a small dedicated capacity estimate. Budget is flexible but we need a 6–12 week measurable window.
[13:58] Dana: Also legal/security checklist before we move data into Redwood-hosted environments.
[14:03] Maya: Understood — we'll trigger the security pack. Jordan, can you share the quant benchmark notebook and a sample pilot plan?
[14:09] Jordan: Yep — I'll upload the notebook and a template plan to the deal in CRM.

[14:20] [14:45] (Jordan runs a quick alternative: hybrid profile preview)
[14:50] Jordan: Hybrid profile: INT8 default but FP8 enforced on top-3 attention layers. Results: p50 105ms, p95 310ms, regressions down to ~0.9% — so better than full INT8.
[15:10] Dana: That hybrid looks promising — could be acceptable if we can identify the critical tokens preserved.

[15:25] Ben: Operationally, will the model variant names change? We need stable routing keys.
[15:30] Jordan: Profiles are versioned and you can pin them to model versions; the API route stays stable — you reference profile_id in the request.

[15:44] [16:05] Samir: Pricing — rough ballpark for a 3-month dedicated pilot?
[16:10] Maya: Rough ranges: dedicated monthly minimum $18k–$45k depending on GPU class and committed throughput. We'll send a more detailed pricing schedule after the call.
[16:20] Samir: Fine.

[16:28] [16:45] (short silence, someone checks notes)
[16:55] Dana: A couple technical Qs — will quantization affect logits calibration, and do you support temperature-sensitive tasks?
[17:02] Jordan: Yes, logits shift can happen; Optimize includes a calibration step where we compare logits distribution and can apply small bias corrections or layer-wise scale to reduce mismatch. For temperature you can tune generation params independently; quant doesn't prevent that but you should eval across your temperature sweep.

[17:30] [18:00] Maya: Ok, wrapping up — quick recap and owners: Jordan to share notebook and demo logs; Maya to send pilot pricing and security pack link; Dana to provide prompt subsets. Pilot kickoff targeted week of Nov 17. Any final questions?
[18:18] Ben: One last infra note — latency from our EU region, can you guarantee region-local nodes?
[18:24] Maya: We have EU regions and can place dedicated pools there. We'll include region options in the pilot plan.

[18:40] [19:00] Samir: Thanks, this was useful. We'll try to get the prompt sets to you next week.
[19:06] Maya: Great, thanks everyone.
[19:10] (Meeting ends, short off-mic chatter)

Notes on transcription: Some words may be transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "rodent" vs "redacted"), occasional speaker labels folded as generic. Deck and notebook links are shorthand and internal references.
